Slovak Industrial Intermediate Prod Sector Hit by Widespread Strike

BRATISLAVA, June 14 – Production at major Slovak industrial intermediate products sites has ground to a halt as hundreds of workers staged a coordinated walkout on Friday, union officials said, prompting concerns over lost output and contract delays.

Employees at four plants operated by firms including Novaprod Solutions, Futura Mat, and SlovaIntermed began industrial action at 6 a.m. local time, citing stalled wage talks and what they called inadequate safety provisions. The Industrial Intermediate Prod Workers Union (IIPWU) said more than 1,200 staff joined the stoppage, affecting facilities in Žilina, Trnava, and Košice.

“All our members are standing together today for fair pay and safer working conditions,” union president Milan Jurcik said in a statement. “We have been negotiating for months with no meaningful progress. This strike is our last resort.”

Management at Novaprod Solutions confirmed operations at its Trnava site were suspended as of Friday morning, with only security staff present. A spokesperson said the company “regrets the disruption” and remains committed to dialogue, but declined to comment on the union’s demands.

The IIPWU said the walkout has halted production of key industrial intermediates, including synthetic resins, specialized polymers, and chemical additives used in downstream manufacturing. At Futura Mat’s Košice plant, production lines stood idle for a second shift, with union officials estimating the facility would miss its daily output target by at least 60%.

Industry analysts warn that, depending on the strike’s duration, the losses could reach millions of euros. “The immediate impact is a standstill in output for these firms, which will have to contend with backlogs and possible penalties for undelivered orders,” said Jozef Liska, an independent sector analyst in Bratislava.

Talks between union leaders and company representatives are scheduled to resume on Monday. Meanwhile, workers have vowed to maintain picket lines until an agreement is reached. “We are ready to stay out as long as it takes,” said Lucia Hanakova, a strike organizer at the Žilina site.

There were no reports of incidents at any of the affected plants.
